target_customer: Video editors, motion designers, musicians and creative professionals who want AI agents to drive their creative tools
problem: Most AI agents target coding. Creative work spans many apps and models, and Voyager gives agents one harness to control them.
business_model: Freemium desktop app with monthly credits, or bring your own Claude or ChatGPT account
product_category: Desktop AI agent harness for creative work

competitors.name: Descript Underlord
competitors.what: Agent that edits video from chat prompts inside Descript

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating agents with many creative apps and 100+ models is broad engineering rather than research, helped by an experienced team.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations are copyable and app makers such as DaVinci Resolve added their own MCP based AI assistance in 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Resolve 21.1 added MCP based agent control in 2026; no acquisition of Voyager found.

market_need_then: Agentic tools were booming in coding in 2026 and a16z published on agentic video editing; creative professionals had no equivalent harness.

branding.domain_note: Uses voyager.so, a .so domain rather than .com; date not found.

identity.visual_style: Product page driven by demos and user posts
identity.voice_and_tone: Taste and vision focused, aimed at creators

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: the faster, cheaper, better harness for creative work
branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt in October 2026; site shows user testimonials from X posts. Shares team lineage with Moda.

brand_strength.rationale: Very new, generic name shared with many companies, some launch buzz.

outcome_analysis: Voyager is a Fall 2026 company from repeat founders behind Moda and Dover, launched as a desktop app in October 2026. It is too new for an outcome. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The main risk is that creative app vendors build native agent control, as DaVinci Resolve did in 2026.
notes: Voyager's own funding not found. A Dealroom listing shows a $125k seed, unverified and not recorded. Moda (a separate company by the same founders) raised a $7.5M seed in March 2026 led by General Catalyst per press releases, not attributed to Voyager. Competitor list is thin because search found mostly vendor blogs. Ravi Parikh's education and employers were not on the sources opened. Completeness pass: the 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom), is undated, names no investors, and the profile is partly AI-generated. A cross-check search found no other source and could not confirm a Y Combinator link beyond the founder's earlier company.
